blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the top of British business, trust is not a soft skill — it is the hard currency in which deals are actually done. Senior people will take a meeting with a firm they trust before they take a cheaper or technically better offer from one they do not. A long-trusted adviser gets the uncomfortable phone call; a newer one gets the polite email.

What gives trust its weight is that it is genuinely hard to fake. It cannot be bought, or manufactured in a quarter, or recovered cleanly once it has been broken. It is built from hundreds of small moments over years: promises kept when no one was watching, honest answers when a comfortable lie was available, quiet credit given to a junior colleague when a senior one could have taken it.

For the leaders who understand this, the implications are practical. Protect the reputation for delivery above short-term wins. Be slow to accept new clients where trust cannot be sensibly built. And treat every small interaction — an email, a reply time, a mention of someone else's work — as a deposit or a withdrawal from an account that almost always decides who you work with in five years.

items.q: According to the text, how is trust best described in senior British business?
options: A soft skill that matters at the margins
The hard currency in which deals are done
A formality handled by the legal team
A useful bonus once a deal is agreed
items.why: "trust is not a soft skill — it is the hard currency in which deals are actually done."

items.q: What does the contrast between "the uncomfortable phone call" and "the polite email" suggest?
options: Email is considered rude at senior levels
Phone calls are reserved for closing deals
Newer advisers communicate more formally by preference
Trusted advisers are given the harder, more candid conversations
items.why: Inferência: quem tem confiança recebe a conversa franca e difícil; quem não tem, fica com o contato distante e cortês.

items.q: Why, according to the text, does trust carry so much weight?
options: Because it can be rebuilt quickly
Because regulators require it
Because it is expensive to acquire
Because it is genuinely hard to fake
items.why: "What gives trust its weight is that it is genuinely hard to fake."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A single strong quarter of revenue can restore a broken reputation
Small, unseen actions accumulate into trust over time
Protecting delivery matters more than short-term wins
Some clients are not worth taking on
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a confiança não se recupera de forma limpa e que a reputação supera ganhos de curto prazo — logo, um trimestre forte não conserta uma reputação quebrada.

items.q: What does treating an interaction as "a deposit or a withdrawal" imply?
options: Every interaction should be billed to the client
Trust behaves like an account that each action raises or depletes
Only financial transactions affect a relationship
Reputations are settled at the end of each year
items.why: Inferência: a metáfora bancária mostra que cada gesto pequeno soma ou subtrai de um saldo de confiança acumulado ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando ao novo sócio por que a firma recusou um cliente lucrativo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
You asked why we walked away from that mandate last quarter — the lucrative one everyone thought we were mad to turn down. Let me be candid with you, because you'll face the same choice yourself before long.

The fee was real, and it was large. But the way that client works, we'd have been pulled into playing our existing relationships off against each other — quiet pressure to favour them, to share things we shouldn't, to bend on terms we'd promised elsewhere. Two of our oldest clients would have felt it within a month, even if they never learned the details.

And that's the calculation. One good quarter against a relationship we've spent eleven years building. It isn't close. The revenue we declined, we can earn again next year. The trust we'd have spent, we cannot buy back at any price.

So the rule here is simple, and I want you to hold it: we're slow to say yes, and we protect the accounts we already have before we chase the ones we don't. Do that consistently, and in five years the right people will still be taking your call.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did the firm turn down the mandate, according to James?
options: It would have corroded trust with existing clients
The fee was too small to justify the work
The team lacked the technical expertise
The client had a poor credit history
items.why: "Two of our oldest clients would have felt it within a month" — a relação teria corroído a confiança com clientes existentes.

items.q: What kind of pressure does James say the client would have applied?
options: Pressure to hire more staff quickly
Pressure to favour them and bend on promises made elsewhere
Pressure to publish confidential results
Pressure to cut fees across the board
items.why: "quiet pressure to favour them… to bend on terms we'd promised elsewhere."

items.q: When James says "It isn't close," what does he mean?
options: The two clients are located near each other
The deadline was very tight
The fee and the relationship were worth roughly the same
The decision was, in fact, an easy one to make
items.why: Inferência: comparando um bom trimestre com onze anos de relação, para ele a escolha é óbvia — não é uma decisão apertada.

items.q: What does James imply is the key difference between the revenue and the trust?
options: Neither is worth protecting carefully
The revenue matters more in the long run
The revenue can be earned again, but the trust cannot be bought back
Both can be recovered with enough time
items.why: "The revenue we declined, we can earn again… The trust we'd have spent, we cannot buy back at any price."

items.q: What is James's main purpose in telling the new partner this story?
options: To criticise the client who was turned away
To pass on a principle the partner will need to apply themselves
To explain a one-off accounting decision
To warn against ever taking large clients
items.why: Inferência: ele diz "you'll face the same choice yourself" e formula uma regra — está transmitindo um princípio, não relatando um caso isolado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "At this level, trust is hard currency, not a nicety." Here, hard currency means…
options: something of real, dependable value that carries weight
physical cash rather than credit
an unpleasant obligation
a foreign exchange contract
items.why: Hard currency = moeda forte: algo de valor real e confiável, que de fato pesa nas decisões.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "You cannot ___ trust in a single quarter; it accrues over years."
options: measure
inherit
manufacture
protect
items.why: To manufacture = fabricar; a lição diz que a confiança não pode ser fabricada num trimestre.

items.q: "She gave an honest answer instead of the comfortable lie the room wanted." A comfortable lie is…
options: an exaggeration used in marketing
a promise made in good faith
a harmless joke to ease tension
a convenient untruth that spares everyone discomfort
items.why: Comfortable lie = mentira conveniente: aquela que evita o desconforto, mas trai a franqueza.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "They chose us over a cheaper bidder because of our ___ built over a decade."
options: reputation for delivery
comfortable lie
polite email
withdrawal
items.why: Reputation for delivery = reputação de entrega, o histórico de cumprir o prometido.

items.q: "A slow reply to a loyal client is a small withdrawal from the account." In this context, a withdrawal is…
options: a refund issued to the client
a decision to leave the relationship
a formal complaint to management
an act that draws down accumulated trust
items.why: Withdrawal = retirada: na metáfora bancária, um gesto que subtrai do saldo de confiança.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre relacionamento e confiança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We decided to walk away from the mandate despite the fee." To walk away from means to…
options: delay the decision
accept it reluctantly
renegotiate the terms
choose to decline or abandon it
items.why: Walk away from = abrir mão, recusar ou abandonar algo por opção.

items.q: "The team agreed the standard but never followed through on it." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
documented it thoroughly
revised it later
delegated it upward
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "A single polished pitch won't move the needle on a decade of doubt." This means it will…
options: settle the matter instantly
cost more than expected
not make a noticeable difference
provoke open conflict
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We're careful about who we take on as a client." To take on means to…
options: recommend to a rival
accept and start working with
confront or challenge
bill in advance
items.why: Take on = assumir, aceitar um novo cliente ou responsabilidade.

items.q: "Over the years those small kindnesses really add up." To add up means to…
options: need to be repaid
cancel each other out
become difficult to track
accumulate into something significant
items.why: Add up = somar-se, acumular-se até virar algo relevante — como os pequenos momentos que constroem a confiança.
